text:
**For most people, Monzo is the best all-round choice for budgeting and savings pots.** Its regular Pots are useful for separating bills and spending money, while Savings Pots earn interest. You can automate saving with recurring transfers and round-ups, and set bills to come from a Pot. Some extras, such as custom categories, are on paid plans.

**Choose Starling if you prefer a straightforward setup.** Its Spaces help you organise money for bills or goals, and virtual cards linked to a Space can help you stick to a spending limit. Check whether the specific Space or saver account you choose earns interest; don’t assume all money set aside does.

**Choose Chase if your priority is savings accounts and round-ups.** Its savings pots are separate saver accounts, and it can round up spending into a savings account. It may be less suited than Monzo if you want detailed day-to-day budgeting.

**My quick take:** Monzo for budgeting plus pots; Starling for simple envelopes and spending control; Chase for a savings-focused setup. Compare the current interest rate, withdrawal rules, and any account fees before moving savings—rates and terms change. Also check FSCS protection and remember the limit applies across eligible deposits you hold with the same banking group.
